function.mechanism: Amphiphilic surfactant that lowers oil-water interfacial tension and stabilizes emulsions/dispersions.

adi.basis: EFSA group ADI for polyoxyethylene sorbitan esters E432-E436 in re-evaluation opinion.

efsa.key_finding: EFSA re-evaluation set a group ADI of 25 mg/kg bw/day and reported refined dietary exposure estimates below the ADI at reported use levels.

fda.notes: Regulated as a permitted direct food additive with specific compositional and use limits; not identified in Part 182/184 GRAS part checks in the 2025-01-01 eCFR title-21 API snapshot.

adi.basis: JECFA ADI 0-25 mg/kg bw, as total polyoxyethylene (20) sorbitan esters.

concerns.summary: Multiple mouse and in vitro studies report microbiome shifts, mucus/barrier disruption, and inflammatory signaling with polysorbate 80 exposure.
Recent preclinical studies report metabolic and senescence-related effects (including maternal-offspring metabolic outcomes) associated with polysorbate 80 exposure.

no_concern_confirmed: No IARC classification was identified for polysorbate 80 in the IARC classified-agents listings checked.
EFSA refined exposure assessment summary reported intake estimates below the ADI at reported use levels.

adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA re-evaluation summary indicates refined mean and high-level exposures did not exceed the 25 mg/kg bw/day group ADI under reported use levels; uncertainty remains for cumulative emulsifier effects and non-standard high-exposure patterns.

risk_assessment.rationale: Regulators continue to permit E433 with ADI/conditions, but converging preclinical mechanistic evidence on gut barrier, microbiome, and metabolic effects supports a cautionary classification above 'limited'.
key_factors: EFSA/JECFA ADIs established and EFSA refined exposure below ADI
FDA permits use under 21 CFR 172.840 with explicit limits
Repeated mechanistic and animal safety signals in recent literature
